_provenance: Simulated illustrative case-study data (100 commuter profiles) calibrated for the Silk Board ↔ Hebbal corridor. Not real respondent research.
datasetTitle: Silk Board ↔ Hebbal Corridor Commuter Experience Case Study
methodology: Simulated cross-sectional commuter profile survey across 100 representative daily bus commuters on the Bengaluru Outer Ring Road.
disclaimer: This research data reflects an illustrative simulated case study. It is provided for operational context and passenger perception analysis only. It is NOT used to calculate vehicle GPS coordinates, timetable headways, passenger loads, bus occupancy, or operational demand.

commuterPainPoints.operationalRelevance: High occupancy (>150% capacity) observed during peak hours at Kadubeesanahalli UP and Marathahalli UP.
Direct consequence of service gaps (e.g. 1,440s gap at Hebbal DOWN following cancelled trips).
External traffic bottlenecks on Outer Ring Road causing irregular dwell and travel times.
Headway coefficient of variation (CV) exceeding 0.40 at key junction monitoring points.
Overcrowded buses unable to board passengers, leading to prolonged roadside passenger waiting.
Heavy dwell delay at Silk Board, Iblur, and Marathahalli signalized intersections.
Successive buses arriving within 75s of each other (e.g. BUS-06 and BUS-07 at Marathahalli UP).
Footboard travel and extreme crush loads resulting from bus bunching and service voids.
Outer Ring Road arterial surface conditions affecting vehicle speed and reliability.
Unplanned vehicle maintenance and driver absenteeism requiring standby relief backfill.
